newsitem.title: CHINA: China stock indices end down on new rumours.
newsitem.headline: China stock indices end down on new rumours.

text.p: China's A and B share indices ended down on Wednesday with fresh rumours of possible further clampdown measures swirling around the markets, brokers said.
The Shanghai B index fell 0.116 points or 0.13 percent to 88.175 points while Shenzhen's B index lost 4.90 points or 2.89 percent to 164.48, with volumes low in both markets.
After the markets closed, Beijing announced new curbs on the trading of shares by state-owned companies, barring them from making "speculative" deals.
State companies that hold shares in listed companies for long-term investment purposes must also file a report with securities exchanges, Beijing said.
The rules also barred listed companies from using funds raised from public offerings to trade in securities and from borrowing from state banks in order to trade stocks.

According to the rumours, new regulations were to be announced soon extending the settlement period for stock trades to three days from the current one day for A shares and immediate settlement for B shares, brokers said.
The intention is to slow down the pace of trading, thereby reducing volatility.

Institutions were seen supporting Shanghai B shares with a heavy index weighting, but they failed to boost retail buying interest due to jitters over possible new steps by Beijing to cool markets, brokers said.
China has already announced a series of measures aimed at cooling its domestic stock markets which have surged more than 50 percent this year.
"A short-lived rebound seems to be ending, and the index will start another downward movement in the next few days," another broker said.
Shanghai Lianhua Fibre was the biggest loser on unpromising prospects, slipping $0.012 or 7.05 percent to $0.158 on volume of 94,000 shares.
Shanghai Jinqiao Export Processing Zone Development was the most actively traded share on profit-taking, falling $0.024 or 3.18 percent to $0.730 on volume of 1.5 million shares.

Shenzhen's B shares fell following tumbles on the A share market. The B index hit an intraday low of 163.06 in the afternoon before recouping some losses just before the close as selling pressure eased, brokers said.
It ended at 164.48, down 4.9 points or 2.89 percent.
The Shenzhen A share index plunged 19.20 points or 3.94 percent to 467.63 on turnover of 8.0 billion yuan.
"The sharp falls in the A share market pushed down B share prices because investors fear that any further falls will spill over into the B share market," an analyst at Shenzhen J&A Securities said.
"But Beijing's clampdown measures are aimed at the A share market, so B share investors do not need to worry about it too much," the analyst said.
Theoretically, B shares can only be traded by foreigners but the rules are sometimes flouted by Chinese investors.
Analysts said Shenzhen investors were largely sticking to the sidelines ahead of a major new B share listing.
The B share market will likely get a boost from an expected strong debut by Nanjing Posts & Telecommunication Equipment Co Ltd's 100 million B share listing on Thursday, they said.
"Nanjing Posts is likely to debut strongly, taking cues from the solid debuts posted by other recent B share listings," an analyst at a major Chinese brokerage said.
In the B share market, the biggest loser was Shenzhen Tellus Machinery, down HK$0.20 or 6.45 percent to close at HK$2.90.

Shanghai's A share index closed down 28.099 points or 1.95 percent to 1,416.119 points on volume of 524.8 million shares worth 7.8 billion yuan. The SSE30 blue chip index fell 18.781 points or 0.46 percent to 4,083.039 points.
